criteria.title: Control plane remains signed Nostr-only
criteria.assertion: Bahia provisioning and lifecycle control for OpenClaw and Metiq must use signed Nostr events only and must not introduce a REST control path.
criteria.expected_result: Operator intent is expressed with signed 31952/5950/1950 events, runtime control uses signed 38384 events, and no external REST agent-management path is added.

criteria.title: Relay handling is event-driven and response-aware
criteria.assertion: SoulFactory must explicitly handle EVENT, EOSE, OK, CLOSED, and AUTH, with scoped subscriptions, dedupe, validation, reconnect/backoff, and no timeout or relay-close terminal inference.
criteria.expected_result: Backfill completion is driven by EOSE, publish success requires accepted OK, CLOSED/AUTH are handled explicitly, duplicates are ignored, and timers are limited to valid backoff/health/rate-limit purposes.

criteria.title: Drafts and read models are reconciled deterministically
criteria.assertion: 31952 is the canonical editable desired spec and 31951 is the authoritative observed/read model, with exact draft event id and spec hash captured for every run.
criteria.expected_result: In-flight draft edits do not mutate active runs; 31951 includes draft, spec-hash, runtime binding, capability ref, deploy status, and last terminal result ref after immediately-known fields are present.

criteria.title: Runtime control contract is shared and complete
criteria.assertion: The shared document defines soulfactory.provision, update, suspend, resume, redeploy, and revoke with methods, tags, params, results, errors, idempotency, trust, validation, and Go/TypeScript compatibility rules.
criteria.expected_result: OpenClaw and Metiq bridge tests can use the same method contract and fixtures without schema forks.

criteria.title: Runtime capability discovery gates target selection
criteria.assertion: OpenClaw and Metiq advertise 30317 capabilities and Bahia selects/provisions only discovered, trusted, compatible runtime targets.
criteria.expected_result: Unsupported or unavailable runtime targets are hidden/rejected; selected targets include capability refs and compatible method/schema versions.

criteria.title: Runtime requests are trusted, validated, idempotent, and correlated
criteria.assertion: 38384 requests must be signed by trusted SoulFactory controller keys, addressed to the target runtime, validated before side effects, idempotent by key, and correlated to 38386 results plus Bahia-facing 6950/7950 events.
criteria.expected_result: Unsigned, stale, duplicate, unauthorized, self-authored, malformed, or misaddressed requests are rejected safely; replay returns the previous result rather than repeating external side effects.

criteria.title: Bahia-facing lifecycle status/result semantics stay backward-compatible
criteria.assertion: Lifecycle actions publish correlated 6950/7950 progress/results with lifecycle tags while preserving legacy event kinds and supporting any legacy KindSoulAction+1 result only as a migration alias.
criteria.expected_result: Existing consumers of 31951/5950/6950/7950/1950 remain valid, new lifecycle consumers use 6950/7950, and migration aliases never become the primary contract.

criteria.title: First vertical slice verifies one OpenClaw and one Metiq lifecycle path
criteria.assertion: The first implementation slice must prove one OpenClaw target and one Metiq target can advertise capability, receive provisioning via 5950 to 38384, publish 38386, produce final 31951/7950, and handle one 1950 to 7950 lifecycle action.
criteria.expected_result: Both runtime families pass the same documented control contract with deterministic event-driven tests and no sleep-based completion assumptions.
